stem: A person with significant dual sensory loss (deaf-blindness) requires access to text from an online portal. Which assistive technology setup allows them to independently read the digital content?

options.text: A screen reader transmitting text data to a refreshable braille display
options.rationale: A screen reader coupled with a refreshable braille device translates on-screen digital text into mechanical braille cells that can be read by touch.

options.text: A personal listening device that reads portal text aloud through an induction loop
options.rationale: Audio output depends on usable hearing, which deaf-blind users cannot rely on for independent text access.

options.text: A media player that displays portal text as synchronized open captions
options.rationale: Captions present text visually, which does not serve a reader with significant vision loss.

options.text: A vibrotactile system that converts portal text into vibration patterns
options.rationale: Vibration patterns can signal events but cannot encode the full text of a document.

explanation: For people who are deaf-blind, touch is often the primary channel for complex information exchange. Screen reader software can route textual and structural digital data directly to a refreshable braille display, enabling independent tactile reading.

references.title: IAAP CPACC Body of Knowledge v4.0
